message.reasoning:
We need to parse the user's request. They want to arrange a flight from SF to LA, date after November 14th, 2024, so presumably November 16th? They want business class, pay with Amex card AMEX123456789. They have access token abc123xyz. Ensure enough funds; they have about $8000.

We need to check flight cost. We can call get_flight_cost with travel_from: SFO (assuming), travel_to: LAX, travel_date: 2024-11-16, travel_class: business. Then we need to get credit card balance. But we don't know card id. We might need to register the card first? The user says they have card number AMEX123456789. We need to register it via register_credit_card. That requires card_number, expiration_date, cardholder_name, cvv. We don't have those details. So maybe we cannot proceed. Alternatively, we could assume card already registered? But we need card_id. We can call get_all_credit_cards to see if card exists. But we don't have access token? We do have access token abc123xyz. So we can call get_all_credit_cards. Then find card matching number? But we don't have card number? Actually we have card number. So we can search. But we don't know expiration_date or cvv. But we can try to register? But we lack expiration_date, cardholder_name, cvv. So can't register. Maybe we can skip registration and just use card_id? But we don't know card_id. So we need to ask for missing info. The user didn't provide expiration_date, cardholder_name, cvv. So we need to ask them. Also we need to confirm flight cost. Let's call get_flight_cost. Then compare with $8000. Then proceed to book_flight. But we need card_id. So we need to get card_id. We can call get_all_credit_cards. Then find card with number AMEX123456789. But we don't have card number stored? Might be stored as masked? Not sure. So better to ask for card details. So we need to ask user for expiration_date, cardholder_name, cvv. Also we need to confirm flight date. They said after Nov 14th, 2024, two days later, so 2024-11-16. We'll ask for confirmation. Then we can proceed.
